reports.title: Lyn Brind: Prevention of future deaths report
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

promises.quote: also plan also commits to reducing average Category 2 ambulance response times to 30 minutes across this fiscal year.
promises.summary: Reduce average Category 2 ambulance response times to 30 minutes

concerns.quote: Evidence was heard that there was a delay in Mrs Brind being transferred from the ambulance to the Emergency Department of the Queen Elizabeth Hospital as there was no space in the hospital
concerns.hazard: delayed transfer of patients from ambulance to emergency department

concerns.quote: physiological observations were not undertaken regularly in accordance with East of England Ambulance Service Trust (EEAST) Guidance and when they were taken, her high NEWS2 score was not escalated to the Hospital Ambulance Navigator who assesses priority for beds in the hospital
concerns.hazard: failure to monitor and escalate patient deterioration

concerns.quote: Further Mrs Brind was not assessed by a Senior Doctor from the Hospital within an hour, in accordance with Hospital protocol
Evidence was heard that there are regularly too many patients in the Emergency Department and so ambulances cannot safely transfer patients into the Emergency Department
at the time of Mrs [name redacted] death, approximately 7 ambulances were waiting to transfer patients into the Emergency Department, Queen Elizabeth Hospital

Further at the time of the inquest there were approximately 140 beds at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital occupied by patients who were medically fit to be discharged, but beds could not be found in the community

reports.title: Dorothy Reid: Prevention of Future Deaths Report
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

promises.quote: The NHS will focus on delivering the following range of practical actions to improve performance in 2025/26: - increasing the proportion of patients seen, treated and discharged in 1 day or less using the principles of same day emergency care (SDEC) - optimising the urgent care offer to meet the needs of their local population, including the use of urgent treatment centres (UTCs) - increasing the percentage of patients discharged by or on day 7 of their admission.
promises.summary: Increase same-day emergency care, optimise urgent care, and boost discharge rates to reduce delays.

concerns.quote: During the course of the evidence it became clear that on both attendances to the emergency department at QEQM she had to wait on a chair as there were no beds. The first attendance led to such a poor experience that she chose not to go back to hospital when an ambulance was called on 31 March 2024. Had she gone to hospital on 31 March 2024 when advised to do so it is likely that her pulmonary embolus would have been diagnosed in the emergency department and treated and she would not have died

Both attendances at the emergency department were on busy shifts but evidence heard from staff was that this was not unusual and the reasons being that beds in the hospital are blocked by patients who are medically fit for discharge
concerns.hazard: hospital bed blocking causing ED overcrowding

concerns.quote: evidence was brought to the courts attention that the President of the Royal College of Emergency Medicine has published an analysis of the impact that this is having and that there are a significant number deaths associated with long waits in the emergency department
concerns.hazard: risk of future deaths from ED overcrowding
